We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). Steps: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide coupling (amide formation). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: Starting from target, we break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline (amine). Then break amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the new alkene). So retrosynthesis: from α,β-unsaturated acid (the side chain) we go back to aldehyde and malonic acid. In our target, the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... The α,β-unsaturated acid is actually after amide formation? Wait: The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... The amide carbonyl is attached to the alkene. The Doebner modification would produce the α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH). Then amide formation converts COOH to CONH-aryl. So retrosynthesis: target -> break amide to give α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break that acid via Doebner to give aldehyde (maybe p-tolyl? Actually the aldehyde is attached to aromatic ring? The α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via the alkene? The structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring (c2) via the alkene substituent. The Doebner would have started from an aldehyde attached to that phenyl ring (i.e., the aldehyde is on the phenyl ring at that position). So the aldehyde is something like c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (para to sulfonamide?). Actually the substituent is at para position relative to sulfonamide? The phenyl ring c2 has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N... So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with CHO group (aldehyde) at that position. So step 2: break the double bond and carboxyl to give aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Step 3: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the first phenyl ring with methyl). So final precursors: 1) p-toluidine (or 4-methyl aniline) for sulfonamide formation? Actually the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the first phenyl ring (with methyl). So the amine part is the aniline (the first phenyl ring). So sulfonyl chloride is the sulfonyl part attached to second phenyl ring (the one bearing the side chain). So we need sulfonyl chloride: Cl-SO2-aryl (the second phenyl). So final precursors: 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine) and 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl (or 4-chlorosulfonyl phenyl) which also has the side chain (aldehyde). Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring which also has the side chain (aldehyde). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is 4-(chlorosulfonyl)-4'-aldehyde phenyl? Wait the sulfonyl chloride attaches to the phenyl ring at position where sulfonamide attaches. The second phenyl ring (c2) has the sulfonyl attached to it (via S=O2) and also the side chain (C=C...). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride substituent (SO2Cl) and the side chain as aldehyde? Actually the side chain is attached via the alkene to the phenyl ring; after Doebner, the aldehyde is attached to the phenyl ring, then Doebner forms the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would have the aldehyde attached to phenyl, and also the sulfonyl chloride group attached to phenyl (para positions). So we need to propose three steps with templates.

We need to produce JSON route with type "mol" root target, children reaction nodes etc.

We need template IDs for each step. We have template 733 for sulfonamide formation (retro: sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + amine). That matches step 1 (retro). Good.

Now need template for amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide). Search for template that does amide formation retro (i.e., amide -> carboxylic acid + amine). Let's search with functional_groups_broken: ["amide"]? Actually broken functional group is amide (since forward forms amide). So broken = amide, formed = carboxylic acid + amine? But we can just search for templates that produce amide from acid+amine. Use functional_groups_broken: ["amide"], functional_groups_formed: ["carboxylic acid", "primary amines"] maybe. Let's try.
